hero.alt: The high-rise skyline of Kuala Lumpur's city centre, Malaysia's main financial district, dominated by the Petronas Twin Towers.

hero.subject: The forested ridges of the Titiwangsa Range, the mountainous backbone of peninsular Malaysia, receding into layered blue ridgelines.
hero.alt: Densely forested green mountain ridges rolling into successive paler blue ridgelines toward the horizon, under a bright blue sky dotted with white clouds.

hero.subject: The broad, silt-brown Kinabatangan River at Bilit, Sabah, flanked by rainforest and riverine vegetation.
hero.alt: A wide muddy-brown tropical river curving between banks lined with dense green rainforest and tall reeds, beneath a bright blue sky with scattered clouds.

hero.subject: Unbroken tropical rainforest canopy stretching to the horizon over the hills of Taman Negara, Malaysia, viewed from Bukit Terisek.
hero.alt: A vast carpet of lush green rainforest canopy covering rolling hills that fade into hazy blue ridges in the distance, under an overcast pale sky.

hero.subject: The red-painted Dutch colonial Stadthuys building and its red clock tower at Dutch Square in Melaka, fronted by a landscaped roundabout of flowers and topiary.
hero.alt: The deep-red Dutch colonial Stadthuys and its red clock tower at Dutch Square in Melaka, with a flower-filled roundabout and directional signpost in front.

hero.subject: A restored stepped candi temple base of reddish laterite blocks at the Bujang Valley (Lembah Bujang) archaeological site in Kedah, standing on a lawn against dense green rainforest.
hero.alt: A restored stepped stone temple base of reddish laterite blocks at the Bujang Valley archaeological site in Kedah, set on a trimmed lawn backed by thick green jungle.

hero.subject: An aerial view of a Malaysian coastal plain where a winding river meets the sea, with dense towns and farmland inland and reclaimed land and mudflats along the shoreline.
hero.alt: An aerial view of a tropical coastal plain where a winding river empties into the sea, towns and farm plots spreading inland and pale reclaimed land edging the shoreline beneath scattered clouds.

hero.alt: A wide view of Kuala Lumpur's dense city skyline under a bright cloudy sky, with the needle-topped KL Tower, clustered skyscrapers and a blue mosque dome rising above green treetops.

hero.subject: The headquarters building of the Immigration Department of Malaysia (Jabatan Imigresen Malaysia) in Putrajaya, with its signage, department crest and flags.
hero.alt: The tall ornate facade of the Immigration Department of Malaysia headquarters in Putrajaya, bearing the Jabatan Imigresen Malaysia name and departmental crest, with flags flying above the entrance.

hero.subject: The Bank Negara Malaysia (central bank) headquarters on Jalan Dato' Onn in Kuala Lumpur.
hero.alt: A large grey modernist concrete office complex of stepped horizontal floors bearing the Bank Negara Malaysia emblem, rising above a screen of green trees and a roadside with hibiscus-flower lamp decorations.

hero.subject: The administrative city of Putrajaya, a federal territory, seen across Putrajaya Lake: the pink-domed Putra Mosque on the left and the green-domed Perdana Putra prime minister's office complex on the right.
hero.alt: Putrajaya across the lake, with the pink-domed Putra Mosque and its tall minaret on the left and the green-domed Perdana Putra government complex on the right under a cloudy sky.

hero.subject: The Melaka Sultanate Palace Museum (Istana Kesultanan Melaka), the wooden replica of the 15th-century sultan's palace in Melaka, Malaysia.
hero.alt: A sprawling timber palace with steeply stacked, multi-tiered grey roofs sits amid manicured tropical gardens, viewed from above with the historic town of Melaka spread out behind it.

hero.subject: The entrance gateway of Fort Cornwallis (built 1786) in George Town, Penang, Malaysia, the largest standing fort of the former British Straits Settlements.
hero.alt: A warmly lit timber-roofed gateway between weathered stone walls glows at dusk, its illuminated sign reading 'Fort Cornwallis 1786 Penang' above an open pathway leading into the fort grounds.

hero.subject: A heavy tropical rainstorm sweeping across a plaza in Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia, an honest stand-in for the torrential rain of Malaysia's monsoon seasons.
hero.alt: Wind-driven rain lashes a cluster of palm trees bending over a deserted, water-slicked city plaza, their fronds streaming sideways beneath a leaden grey sky as high-rise towers fade into the downpour.

hero.subject: Istana Iskandariah, the official royal palace of the Sultan of Perak, in Bukit Chandan, Kuala Kangsar, Perak, Malaysia.
hero.alt: A white royal palace crowned with gilded onion domes rises behind an ornate black-and-white perimeter fence on a green hillside under a clear sky.

hero.subject: Istana Bandar (Istana Sultan Alaeddin), a historic royal palace of the Selangor Sultanate in Kampung Bandar, Kuala Langat, Selangor, Malaysia.
hero.alt: A two-storey whitewashed colonial-era palace with a red tiled roof and a wide balustraded verandah stands on a manicured lawn fringed by coconut palms.

hero.subject: The Sultan Abu Bakar State Mosque, the royal state mosque of Johor, in Johor Bahru, Johor, Malaysia.
hero.alt: A grand white Victorian-style mosque with twin spired towers and blue-black domes rises above landscaped gardens beneath an overcast sky.

hero.subject: The Sultan Abu Bakar Museum (the former royal residence, now the royal museum) in Pekan, Pahang, seat of the Pahang Sultanate.
hero.alt: A grand white colonial-era palace with red-tiled roofs and Jawi script above its arched entrance, mirrored in a still reflecting pool flanked by crane sculptures under a cloudy sky.

hero.subject: The Malaysian national flag (Jalur Gemilang) flying from the flagpole at Dataran Merdeka (Merdeka Square), Kuala Lumpur.
hero.alt: The red-and-white striped Malaysian flag with its blue canton bearing a yellow crescent and fourteen-point star streams out fully from a tall white flagpole against a blue sky.

hero.subject: The Zahir Mosque (Masjid Zahir) in Alor Setar, Kedah, one of Malaysia's oldest and grandest royal mosques, associated with the Kedah Sultanate.
hero.alt: A majestic white Moorish mosque crowned by clustered black onion domes and slender minarets, its ornate arched facade rising above an open plaza beneath dramatic clouds.

hero.subject: Istana Lama Seri Menanti, the historic four-storey all-timber Minangkabau-style royal palace at Seri Menanti, Negeri Sembilan.
hero.alt: A grand dark-timber palace crowned with a tall tiered tower and sweeping shingled roofs stands against forested hills beyond a wide green field.

hero.subject: Istana Maziah, the royal palace of the Terengganu Sultanate in Kuala Terengganu.
hero.alt: A cream-and-gold colonial-style palace with red-tiled turrets and arched arcades sits bathed in sunlight under a deep blue sky beyond a broad lawn.

hero.subject: Istana Jahar, the ornate historic royal palace in Kota Bharu, now the Kelantan Royal Ceremonies Museum (Muzium Adat Istiadat).
hero.alt: An ornate black timber palace with yellow pillars, carved fascias and tiered roofs rises behind a vintage horse carriage parked on a circular brick forecourt.

hero.subject: The ornate ceremonial main gatehouse of the new Istana Negara (National Palace) on Jalan Tuanku Abdul Halim, Kuala Lumpur, official residence of the Yang di-Pertuan Agong.
hero.alt: The grand arched gatehouse of the National Palace, crowned with twin gold onion domes and a gilded gate bearing the royal crest, stands against a clear blue sky.

hero.subject: Istana Kenangan in Kuala Kangsar, Perak, a historic woven-bamboo-walled timber royal palace now serving as the Perak Royal Museum.
hero.alt: A traditional Malay timber palace with woven bamboo walls, steep tiled roofs and carved gables stands beneath a bright sky.

hero.subject: The Sultan Abdul Samad Building in Kuala Lumpur, the Moorish-style former Federated Malay States government secretariat on Dataran Merdeka.
hero.alt: A long Moorish facade of ochre brick and white arches crowned by copper domes and a tall central clock tower under a blue sky.

hero.subject: Malaysia Day celebrations in Singapore on 16 September 1963, when Malaya, Singapore, Sabah and Sarawak joined to form Malaysia.

hero.alt: A grand colonial mansion of cream walls and a red-tiled roof set among manicured lawns and tropical greenery.

hero.subject: A monumental granite Buddha statue unearthed at Bukit Seguntang, the sacred hill at the heart of Srivijaya's capital at Palembang in Sumatra, now displayed in a Palembang museum.
hero.alt: A weathered grey granite Buddha, legs lost, standing serene against green foliage on the sacred hill of Srivijaya's old capital.

hero.subject: The reconstructed Candi Bukit Batu Pahat (c. 6th century) in the Bujang Valley, Kedah, a Hindu-Buddhist temple of the early Kedah civilisation of the same region and era associated with Langkasuka, whose own capital site remains archaeologically unconfirmed.
hero.alt: A low stepped stone temple plinth on a grassy clearing framed by palms and green hills in the Bujang Valley.

hero.subject: An eighth-to-ninth-century bronze Avalokiteshvara found at Bidor, Perak in 1936, now in the National Museum, Kuala Lumpur, a genuine Perak Hindu-Buddhist artefact of the era linked to the Gangga Negara legend, not an object tied to the unconfirmed kingdom itself.
hero.alt: A slender, many-armed bronze bodhisattva figure, green with age, lit against a dark museum backdrop.

hero.subject: Tunku Abdul Rahman raises his hand during the proclamation of Malaya's independence on 31 August 1957.
hero.alt: Tunku Abdul Rahman stands before a crowd, hand raised, at the historic 1957 Merdeka independence proclamation.

hero.subject: A Malaysian Army music band marches on parade during the 55th National Day Parade at Merdeka Square, Kuala Lumpur.
hero.alt: Uniformed military bandsmen march in formation past spectators during Malaysia's Merdeka Day parade at Dataran Merdeka.

hero.subject: The Petronas Twin Towers rise above the Kuala Lumpur skyline, the emblem of Malaysia's modernisation drive.
hero.alt: The gleaming Petronas Twin Towers soar above the Kuala Lumpur skyline under a bright sky.

hero.subject: The Johor-Singapore Causeway, the physical land link across the Straits of Johor connecting Malaysia and Singapore, which separated from Malaysia in 1965.
hero.alt: The Johor-Singapore Causeway stretches low across the shimmering Straits of Johor, carrying road and rail toward the Singapore shoreline on the horizon as seen from the Malaysian side.

hero.subject: Bangunan Parlimen in Kuala Lumpur, the Parliament House of Malaysia, embodying the constitutional order the Reid Commission's 1957 constitution created.
hero.alt: Malaysia's Parliament House stands in landscaped grounds in Kuala Lumpur, its slender office tower and sculptural ribbed legislative chamber gleaming in bright daylight.

hero.subject: The federal government precinct at Putrajaya, with the rose-domed Putra Mosque and the Perdana Putra complex, representing national development.

hero.subject: Tunku Abdul Rahman, the first Prime Minister of Malaya and Malaysia, who led the country to independence in 1957 and governed until 1970.
